agent.problem: Discovery questions dominate the stop. Cards 2, 5, 9, 11, 13 and 19 do not give the baker enough earlier context to reason out their answers, and cards 4 and 7 also largely ask the baker to predict the next detail. A few discovery questions are allowed, but here at least six of the ten choices depend on luck or prior Bible knowledge rather than the earlier cards.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Card 1 says only that Joseph is a rich man from Arimathea. It gives no basis for reasoning out his relationship to Jesus, so the baker must guess disciple rather than cousin or neighbor. The blank supplies an unseen detail instead of testing a meaning supported by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Card 18 says only that the group goes to the tomb. Sealing, chaining and bracing are all plausible ways to secure a stone, and nothing in the earlier cards distinguishes them, so the baker must guess the unseen wording.
